title: Multi-alert correlation
summary: Alert A on SRV-WEB-04 is failed-login noise - INCONCLUSIVE. Alert B later, same source IP, opens its own case. While working case B the agent finds case A via get_related_alerts and correlates. Case A then reconsiders on the strength of case B.

conclusions.label: initial
conclusions.hypothesis: The attack (MySQL port 3306 enumeration) succeeded if the attacker bypassed authentication and accessed or exfiltrated data from SRV-WEB-04's MySQL instance.
conclusions.sufficiency: I have sufficient evidence to classify this as an attack that was ATTEMPTED but did NOT SUCCEED. The host was vulnerable via MySQL 5.7.25 (inside CVE-2023-21980's range), but the attacker was blocked at the authentication layer — all connections were refused or access-denied, no queries executed, no data exfiltrated, and packet metadata confirms no meaningful data transfer. The 'low' severity label from the sensor is consistent with this finding: the attack was noisy but unsuccessful.
conclusions.disconfirming_evidence_checked: I checked for evidence that would falsify the 'attack failed' hypothesis: (1) any successful authentication or query execution in server logs — none found, all denied; (2) any exfiltration in packet metadata — exfil_indicators is false and no meaningful data returned; (3) any related alerts corroborating success — none exist for this asset. All disconfirming checks came back negative, supporting the conclusion that the attack did not succeed.
